title: Composed VeRA Mirror views and task arithmetic

model.shared_adapter_basis: one normalized rank-1 projection K=u u^T, so K^2=K

hypothesis: A one-coordinate Mirror composition law alpha_comp=alpha1+alpha2+alpha1*alpha2 can represent sequential composition of two shared-basis VeRA views more compactly and accurately than ordinary task-vector/scaling addition alpha1+alpha2.
physical_object: one shared rank-1 projection basis u and deterministic identity base
mirror_coordinate: one composed scalar address over the shared operator
logical_multiplicity: one composed adapter function from two VeRA task views
controls: ordinary task arithmetic / sum of VeRA scales
sequential application of both VeRA views
independent explicit composed matrix upper control

development.allowed: validate algebraic identity, task/data shapes, serializer and timing; no hyperparameter selection

storage.authority: Canonical packed little-endian binary inference payload, including fixed 8-byte header, shared basis vector, task code(s), or explicit matrix.

success_gate: Mirror composed NRMSE <=1e-6 and uses <=80% of two separate VeRA codes+sequential path payload bytes in every fresh world; report generic product-law equality, which if matched prevents Mirror-specific novelty claim.
failure_gate: Ordinary scale addition is within 5% NRMSE of exact composition or generic scalar product law matches Mirror without a byte/compute penalty, for Mirror-specific value.
boundaries: One rank-1 idempotent basis and scalar coefficients only; no general multi-adapter or NLP composition claim.
This tests function composition algebra; composition count is not independent capacity.
The generic scalar product-law control is intentionally the cheapest alternative.

amendment_before_fresh.reason: torch.save overhead erased the one-vs-two scalar byte distinction in development.
amendment_before_fresh.change: Use fixed-header packed binary payload and decode each stored artifact before evaluation.

development_summary.interpretation: Composed law restores exact sequential behavior, but generic product-law control is identical; 1-code payload is only 2.8% smaller than two-scale sequential.

result_summary.interpretation: The nonlinear composition term restores sequential function behavior and halves the application steps, but the generic scalar product law is identical and the payload saves only 2.8% versus storing two scales.
